messages:
miguel: Quick sanity check — /v2/generate sometimes returns Content-Type: text/plain for structured outputs (we expect application/json). Getting errors in node SDK parsing. Anyone else seeing this after the canary? (curl example attached)

anna: Noticed similar in local tests. Can you paste curl + response headers?

miguel: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"...","format":"json"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate

Response headers show: Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

chris: Hmm that's the new streaming tweak? Deploy bot shows canary rolled 03:14 UTC.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy v2-generate -> 2026-03-17T03:14Z (50% traffic)

elena: Possible root cause: middleware falling back to plain text when structured-output serialization raises an exception (null field in model output). Recommend adding JSON Schema validation in runtime to force 500 and fallback to stable model instead of emitting text.

anna: Short-term fix: SDK should attempt parsing when content-type is application/json OR when body starts with '{' or '['. I'll open a tiny PR.

miguel: Also, what's our desired contract for nullable vs omitted keys in structured outputs? Current doc ambiguous.

elena: Contract: stable keys should be present unless explicitly optional in schema. For optional things, prefer omitting rather than null for backward compatibility. I'll add a bullet in the API contract doc.

chris: +1. For streaming ndjson we should keep each event JSON-valid; don't emit plain-text fallback in the stream.

miguel: thx. @anna mention me on the SDK PR. I'll add a canary smoke test that asserts Content-Type == application/json for structured routes.

anna: will do. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234

miguel: Closing loop: canary rollback if we still see text/plain after next deploy? plan to monitor.

sre-oncall: I'll add an alert on 5xx when parsed json fails and a metric for content-type mismatches.

miguel: perfect :thumbsup:
